analysis:
PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Six positions are open, which is already above the 3-5 concentrated-position target. Available cash is $18,219 but deployable headroom for new buys is only $13,200 — insufficient to size a new name properly per the 1-2% equity-heat rule without crowding the book further. The historical track record (22.2% win rate, 0.08x profit factor, Sortino -3.97) is a clear signal that the strategy has been over-trading or entering too early; the corrective action is greater selectivity and patience, not adding a seventh name.

EXISTING POSITION FLAGS:
• LII (-6.61%): Most at-risk holding. Stock is well below the original average cost of $575.57 (now $537.50), the SMA50 slope is positive but price is only +2.9% above SMA50 — a further leg down could trigger a stop. Critically, LII reports earnings July 29 (19 days). Holding through earnings with a -6.61% unrealized loss and unclear macro backdrop is asymmetric to the downside. Recommend tightening the stop to 1.5x ATR (~$19.35) below current price, i.e., ~$518, and being prepared to exit pre-earnings if the stock fails to hold $530.
• AMP (+11.22%): The clear winner. Thesis intact — quality financial services with strong ROE. No action needed; let it run with a trailing stop below the SMA50.
• WDAY (+2.15%): In the candidate list with basing uptrend. Thesis intact; small position. Hold.
• A (+2.99%), CI (+3.52%): Both modestly profitable, no thesis break visible.
• FDS (-1.60%): Small loss, within noise. Monitor.

NEW TRADES: No new positions are being proposed this cycle. Reasons: (1) 6 positions already exceed the 3-5 target; (2) $13,200 headroom cannot fund a properly sized seventh position without concentration risk or underweighting; (3) the most attractive candidate (VEEV — quality, basing at 25% of 52w range, no earnings until Sep 2, PEG 0.85, positive EPS revisions) is genuinely interesting but would require ~$13K for even a minimum-heat position, leaving zero buffer for thesis-break exits on existing names; (4) multiple existing holdings face earnings in the next 12-19 days (PHM July 22, COF July 21, LII July 29) creating near-term binary risk across the book. The honest, evidence-based call is to let existing stops work, prune LII if it deteriorates, and preserve the cash position. When one or two existing positions close out, VEEV or BX (after earnings July 23) become natural candidates for properly sized entries. Cash is not failure — it is discipline.
